grades.quote: waiting for a condition variable should always be done using a loop, because when the thread finishes waiting, it may not be the first to acquire the mutex.
grades.reason: Directly explains why a condition-variable wait belongs in a loop: the woken thread may not be first to acquire the mutex, so the condition may no longer hold, and spurious wakeups can occur.

grades.quote: they will all try to acquire the condition lock and re-check the condition; in many cases only one will be able to do anything useful
grades.reason: Gives part of the rationale: after a wakeup, several waiters re-check the condition and the ones that find it false go back to sleep. It also notes that sleeping processes can be woken before the awaited event happens. It does not state the while-loop rule for condition variables directly.
Describes the RISC-V Zawrs wait-on-reservation-set instructions for low-power polling. It says nothing about why condition-variable waits go in a while loop.
This is a general chapter introduction to synchronization. It mentions condition variables only in passing and never explains why the wait should be in a loop.
